newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds end stronger on wages data, euro issuance.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds end stronger on wages data, euro issuance.

* Yields close lower after weaker than expected wages data
* Politics seen the only obstacle to Reserve Bank easing
* Continuing euro, dual currency issuance underpins market
New Zealand debt securities rallied on weaker-than-anticipated wages data on Tuesday, with yields closing the session between six and 10 basis points lower across the curve.
Statistics New Zealand said ordinary time wages rose 3.4 percent in the August year, in line with forecasts, but private sector earnings rose only 3.7 percent against market forecasts of 4.2 percent.
Economists said the data showed inflationary pressures in the labour market had peaked, paving the way for an easing in monetary policy over the next six months.

"Obviously that takes a little bit of the acid off the Reserve Bank, gives it the chance to ease a little bit earlier than might otherwise be the case...the market reacted quite positively to that," one bond dealer remarked.
But he added: "Nothing is going to happen until the bank sees what comes out of the coalition talks."
A new administration has yet to emerge from inconclusive elections last month and the main political parties are still in negotiations to form a coalition government.

Whatever the outcome, all parties have conceded that government spending will rise. Reserve Bank governor Don Brash last week cautioned against looser fiscal conditions, saying this would put upward pressure on interest rates and the dollar.

Bond traders said good buying interest in the middle of the yield curve, especially in the 02/00s, and the currency's steady climb higher throughout the day suggested more eurokiwi issues were on the cards.
"Just looking at the currency and looking at the bonds, I wouldn't be surprised if we see another one tomorrow morning," a dealer said.

The World Bank issued a NZ$100 million euro bond last night. There was also a 5 billion yen samurai issued by the Council of Europe. ---------------------------------------------------------------- Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD
